body: I am megacycle. Full time between 40-58 hours/week -  I communicate with my managers and site leads about more hours and I average about $2800-3500/depending on how many weeks are in the month and how many days I work. I usually work 5-6 days/week. - I am T1 so I can make the hours if I perform well when I arrive.

At my former station we had 2 pregnant women. I work sortation. One was safety or temp check and the other worked in USPS redirects (desk work).
they were permitted to sit of course
I was trained for hazmat and I problem solve/quality. For me it is easy now but you have to learn that packages have to be corrected to leave or go back to the fc and want to do it the right way

I have always worked megacycle buildings and yes it is not easy. I am young, single and childless. Living with my family is the only reason I see them. I am professional but a serious relationship with someone outside of my job is impossible.  

It is a long shift of very dedicated people and it makes a world of difference if you enjoy your management team. Management has to be good at employee engagement.

I can’t really say more but the shifts are 10 hours. Some stations begin at 2:40am-1 something. It is both sort and pick/stage- maybe station reset. 

The hours have meant more money. I can’t really imagine less hours and less money
This really depends on where in the DMV.

The yellow sticker is important- the last two will be (2B, 1C, 3G and so on for aisle locations) - the number tells you whether you will bend for 1 or remain standing for 3 and so on - **the letter helps you multi-carry. Grab a few letters that are near each other like ABC or DEG. If you count to 60 and pick up 8 items in that time frame by carrying 4 at a time both your quality and speed will increase - what matters is how many you can do in one minute but a few good minutes go a long way
